rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi connects the preceding pronouns with Allah in the description of the unseen and visible; taking the possessive as Allah makes the clause mean that Allah has guardians following in succession.
rows.anchor: وقيل على اسم الله في عالم الغيب والشهادة ، والمعنى : لله معقبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may derive from an assimilated form of معتقبات, or from عقب, something that follows on the heels of what came before; both derivations yield the same sense.
rows.anchor: أن يكون أصل هذه الكلمة معتقبات فأدغمت التاء في القاف كقوله

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The famous majority view identifies the guardians as angels, either because night and day angels succeed one another or because they follow and record human deeds; they are the angels of both shifts.
rows.anchor: المشهور الذي عليه الجمهور أن المراد منه الملائكة الحفظة وإنما صح وصفهم بالمعقبات

rows.speaker: عثمان رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Uthman asked the Prophet how many angels accompany a person; the Prophet described recorders of good and evil and other angels guarding the person, ten at a time, replaced between night and day for twenty total.
rows.anchor: روي عن عثمان رضي الله عنه أنه قال : يا رسول الله أخبرني عن العبد كم معه من ملك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says angels of night and day alternate and meet at the dawn and afternoon prayers; Razi links this to the prayer times in 17:78.
rows.anchor: يتعاقب فيكم ملاكئة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj equates the guardians with the two recorders, one on the right writing good deeds and one on the left writing sins, as in 50:17.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : هو مثل قوله تعالى : { عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد }

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says each servant has an angel protecting him from jinn, humans, and vermin while asleep and awake.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : ما من عبد إلا وله ملك يحفظه من الجن والإنس والهوام في نومه ويقظته

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the feminine plural refers to male angels: ملائكة معقبة is pluralized as معقبات, and the masculine يحفظونه supports this reading.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : المعقبات ذكران جمع ملائكة معقبة ، ثم جمعت معقبة بمعقبات

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the feminine form reflects the angels’ large number, like نسابة and علامة, which are feminine forms used of a male.
rows.anchor: قول الأخفش : إنما أنثت لكثرة ذلك منها ، نحو : نسابة ، وعلامة ، وهو ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels surround the person moving secretly at night or openly by day and fully count all his deeds and words, leaving nothing unrecorded.
rows.anchor: أن المستخفي بالليل والسارب بالنهار قد أحاط به هؤلاء المعقبات فيعدون عليه أعماله وأقواله بتمامها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view is that the guardians protect a person from every danger in front and behind, the directions from which a daytime traveler watches for threats.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل المراد يحفظونه من جميع المهالك من بين يديه ومن خلفه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’s first parsing places من أمر الله with معقبات by advancing the phrase: the angels are guardians from God’s command.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : أنه على التقديم والتأخير والتقدير : له معقبات من أمر الله يحفظونه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’s second parsing supplies an omitted noun: the protection is from God’s command, with its noun deleted and its predicate retained.
rows.anchor: أن فيه إضمارا أي ذلك الحفظ من أمر الله أي مما أمر الله به فحذف الاسم وأبقى خبره

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reads من as باء, so the angels guard by God’s command and aid; creatures cannot protect anyone from what God decrees against him.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن الأنباري أن كلمة ( من ) معناها الباء والتقدير : يحفظونه بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that assigning guardians to people is not implausible: astrologers assign daily and nightly governance to separate planets and talismanists speak of a complete natural spirit for each person.
rows.anchor: المنجمين اتفقوا على أن التدبير في كل يوم لكوكب على حدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the philosophical account Razi cites, human spirits differ in character, celestial spirits are stronger, and each human group shares a nature with a corresponding celestial spirit that guides and protects it; this makes the scriptural teaching acceptable.
rows.anchor: أن الأرواح البشرية مختلفة في جواهرها وطبائعها فبعضها خيرة ، وبعضها شريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One benefit of angelic guardians is that devils invite people to evil and disobedience while angels invite them to good works and obedience.
rows.anchor: أن الشياطين يدعون إلى الشرور والمعاصي ، وهؤلاء الملائكة يدعون إلى الخيرات والطاعات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid’s reported benefit is that each servant has an angel protecting him from jinn, humans, and vermin during sleep and wakefulness.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : ما من عبد إلا ومعه ملك يحفظه من الجن والإنس والهوام في نومه ويقظته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sudden inward impulse may later prove beneficial or harmful; Razi identifies the helpful impulse with an angel guiding to good and the harmful one with Satan leading astray.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الملك الهادي والثاني هو الشيطان المغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that exalted angels witness, count, and write one’s deeds restrains sin through shame; belief that the deeds are recorded makes the deterrent stronger.
rows.anchor: وإذا علم أن الملائكة يكتبونها كان الردع أكمل

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: The theologians say deeds are written so the records can be weighed and the balance reveal to creation whether a person belongs to Paradise or its opposite.
rows.anchor: قال المتكلمون : الفائدة في تلك الصحف وزنها ليعرف رجحان إحدى الكفتين على الأخرى

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi objects that the scale is not needed to establish a person’s fate, since each person knows before death at the moment of witnessing; he allows that the public result may bring joy to God’s friends and the converse to His enemies.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا بعيد لأن الأدلة قد دلت على أن كل واحد قبل مماته عند المعاينة يعلم أنه من السعداء

rows.speaker: حكماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Islamic philosophers interpret writing as conventional marks that identify meanings; writing would be stronger and more complete if its marks directly signified the meanings’ essences.
rows.anchor: قول حكماء الإسلام أن الكتابة عبارة عن نقوش مخصوصة وضعت بالاصطلاح لتعريف المعاني المخصوصة

rows.speaker: حكماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Repeated actions produce a deep, lasting disposition: a disposition formed by beneficial spiritual deeds brings great joy after death, while a harmful one causes great distress.
rows.anchor: حصل في نفسه بسبب تكررها ملكة قوية راسخة ، فإن كانت تلك الملكة ملكة سارة بالأعمال النافعة

rows.speaker: حكماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Because each repeated act contributes to a lasting disposition, every human movement or stillness leaves some degree of felicity or misery in the soul; this is what recording deeds means on this account, if the guardians are angels.
rows.anchor: لا يحصل للإنسان لمحة ولا حركة ولا سكون ، إلا ويحصل منه في جوهر نفسه أثر من آثار السعادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: A second interpretation transmitted from Ibn Abbas takes the passage to mean that God knows secret and open actions equally: night fugitives and daytime travelers with guards cannot escape His decree.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو أيضا منقول عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، واختاره أبو مسلم الأصفهاني المراد : أنه يستوي في علم الله تعالى السر والجهر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim chooses the interpretation that human guards and helpers cannot save rulers or their masters from God’s decree, unlike the majority’s angelic-guardian interpretation.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا منقول عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، واختاره أبو مسلم الأصفهاني المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading المعقب means a helper: reciprocal watching makes each person’s perception follow the other’s, but such guards cannot avert God’s decree.
rows.anchor: والمعقب العون ، لأنه إذا أبصر هذا ذاك فلا بد أن يبصر ذاك هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns sultans, princes, and leading people to seek safety through God’s protection rather than relying on helpers, since God’s judgment cannot be repelled.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الكلام بعث السلاطين والأمراء والكبراء على أن يطلبوا الخلاص من المكاره عن حفظ الله

rows.speaker: جميع المفسرين
rows.claim: All commentators take God’s changing a people to mean removing their blessings through punishment only after they commit sins and corruption.
rows.anchor: كلام جميع المفسرين يدل على أن المراد لا يغير ما هم فيه من النعم بإنزال الانتقام إلا بأن يكون منهم المعاصي والفساد

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says the apparent wording permits only a change into punishment, since God can initiate other acts without a prior change by people and initially bestowed religious and worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : والظاهر لا يحتمل إلا هذا المعنى لأنه لا شيء مما يفعله تعالى سوى العقاب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some connect this statement with 13:6: God sends annihilating punishment only when people are known to persist in disbelief and sin; if some or their descendants will believe, He does not destroy them utterly.
rows.anchor: فبعضهم قال هذا الكلام راجع إلى قوله : { ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة }

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others take the statement generally: when a people extensively corrupt their way of worshipping God, He removes their blessings and sends kinds of punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل الكلام يجري على إطلاقه ، والمراد منه أن كل قوم بالغوا في الفساد وغيروا طريقتهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say believers mixed among corrupt people may also be caught up in the collective punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن المؤمن الذي يكون مختلطا بأولئك الأقوام فربما دخل في ذلك العذاب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reports the Prophet warning that when people see an oppressor but do not restrain him, God may soon subject them all to punishment.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي بكر رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي والقاضي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba’i and al-Qadi use the verse to argue that God does not punish the children of polytheists for their parents’ sins, since the children did not change their state from blessing to punishment.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى لا يعاقب أطفال المشركين بذنوب آبائهم ، لأنهم لم يغيروا ما بأنفسهم من نعمة فيغير الله حالهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي والقاضي
rows.claim: They also argue that the verse refutes the determinists’ claim that God initiates a servant’s misguidance and abandonment at puberty, which would be a greater punishment without any prior change by the servant.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على بطلان قول المجبرة إنه تعالى يبتدىء العبد بالضلال والخذلان أول ما يبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that although this verse seems to put God’s change after the servant’s act, 76:30 puts the servant’s willing after God’s will, so the two claims conflict.
rows.anchor: إلا أن قوله تعالى : { وما * يشآءون * إلا أن يشاء الله }

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi’s school cites the promise that no one can repel God’s intended harm to argue that a servant is not independent in action: independent ability to believe would let him overturn God’s judgment of a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: فقد احتج أصحابنا به على أن العبد غير مستقل في الفعل

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the guardians avail nothing against God’s decree.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك عن ابن عباس : لم تغن المعقبات شيئا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata transmits from Ibn Abbas the gloss that no one can repel God’s punishment or overturn His judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه : لا راد لعذابي ولا ناقض لحكمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase means they have no protector besides God to manage their affairs and prevent the punishment.
rows.anchor: أي ليس لهم من دون الله من يتولاهم ، ويمنع قضاء الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi parses “those who believe” as an appositive of “whoever turns back” in the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: أن قوله { الذين آمنوا } بدل من قوله { من أناب }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when these believers hear the Qur’an, their hearts become humble and tranquil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد إذا سمعوا القرآن خشعت قلوبهم واطمأنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ trembling in 8:2 concerns remembered punishment and fear of sin, while tranquility here concerns the promise of reward and mercy; each arises in its proper context.
rows.anchor: أنهم إذا ذكروا العقوبات ولم يأمنوا من أن يقدموا على المعاصي فهناك وصفهم بالوجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reconciliation is that the Qur’an’s miraculous character reassures believers that Muhammad is truly God’s prophet, while uncertainty about the completeness of their obedience produces fear.
rows.anchor: أن علمهم بكون القرآن معجزا يوجب حصول الطمأنينة لهم في كون محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم نبيا حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reconciliation is that believers are certain of God’s and Muhammad’s truthfulness yet fear whether they have performed enough obedience and avoided the sins that incur punishment.
rows.anchor: أنه حصلت في قلوبهم الطمأنينة في أن الله تعالى صادق في وعده ووعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes three classes of beings: God acts without being affected, bodies are affected without acting, and spiritual beings both act and are affected; spirits receive divine effects when turned toward God and long to govern bodies when turned toward the physical world.
rows.anchor: أن الموجودات على ثلاثة أقسام : مؤثر لا يتأثر ، ومتأثر لا يؤثر ، وموجود يؤثر في شيء ويتأثر في شيء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say طوبى is not Arabic and means Paradise in Abyssinian or Indian, or a garden in Indian; Razi rejects this because the Qur’an is Arabic and the word has an evident Arabic derivation.
rows.anchor: أن هذه اللفظة ليست عربية ، ثم اختلفوا فقال بعضهم : طوبى اسم الجنة بالحبشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the non-Arabic interpretation weak because the Qur’an is Arabic and طوبى is plainly derived from Arabic.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف ، لأنه ليس في القرآن إلا العربي لا سيما واشتقاق هذا اللفظ من اللغة العربية ظاهر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf parses الذين آمنوا as the subject and طوبى لهم as its predicate; طوبى means “you have attained goodness” and can be accusative or nominative.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : { الذين آمنوا } مبتتدأ و { طوبى لهم } خبره

rows.speaker: مكوزة الأعرابي
rows.claim: Mukawwiz the Bedouin read طوبى as طيبى.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مكوزة الأعرابي ' طيبى لهم '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حسن مآب means a good return and abode; the promise of supreme bliss encourages obedience and warns against disobedience.
rows.anchor: فالمراد حسن المرجع والمقر . وكل ذلك وعد من الله بأعظم النعيم ترغيبا في طاعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada take كذلك أرسلناك to compare Muhammad’s mission with the prophets sent to earlier nations.
rows.anchor: فقيل أرسلناك كما أرسلنا الأنبياء قبلك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم ، وهو قول ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation compares Muhammad’s revealed book, which he recites, with the books given to earlier peoples, asking what further sign his opponents could demand.
rows.anchor: وقيل كما أرسلنا إلى أمم وأعطيناهم كتبا تتلى عليهم ، كذلك أعطيناك هذا الكتاب وأنت تتلوه عليهم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads “such sending” as a mission of distinction and excellence over other missions: Muhammad is sent to the last community and is the final prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشاف ' كذلك أرسلناك ' أي مثل ذلك الإرسال ' أرسلناك '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mission is to recite the great Book revealed to Muhammad to people who reject the All-Merciful, whose encompassing mercy supplies their blessings, including the sending of the Prophet and the miraculous Qur’an.
rows.anchor: فالمراد : لتقرأ عليهم الكتاب العظيم الذي أوحينا إليك { وهم يكفرون بالرحمن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains “He is my Lord” as affirming the one God, “in Him I trust” as seeking His help to defeat the opponents, and “to Him is my return” as seeking help to persevere against them.
rows.anchor: عليه توكلت } في نصرتي عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion identifies the rejecter of the name al-Rahman as Abd Allah b. Umayya al-Makhzumi, who claimed to know Allah but not al-Rahman and associated that name with Musaylima; Razi links the reply to 17:110 and 25:60.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزل قوله { وهم يكفرون بالرحمن } في عبد الله بن أمية المخزومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion is the Hudaybiyya treaty: Quraysh objected to writing Muhammad as God’s Messenger and to “In the name of God, the All-Merciful,” asking instead for their familiar wording.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه عليه السلام حين صالح قريشا من الحديبية كتب ' هذا ما صالح عليه محمد رسول الله '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the two reported occasions are intended, the opponents rejected applying the name al-Rahman to God, rather than rejecting God Himself.
rows.anchor: إذا حملناه على هاتين الروايتين كان معناه أنهم كفروا بإطلاق هذا الإسم على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other scholars say they rejected God Himself, either by denying Him or by associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل كفروا بالله إنا جحدا له وإما لإثباتهم الشركاء معه

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi prefers the second view because the apparent wording says they disbelieved in God, and “al-Rahman” denotes God Himself rather than merely His name, as “they denied Muhammad” denotes the person.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذا القول أليق بالظاهر ، لأن قوله تعالى { وهم يكفرون بالرحمن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reports that Meccans asked Muhammad to move the mountains, make rivers for farming, resurrect relatives to question them, or subject the wind to them as for Solomon; Abd Allah b. Umayya said he was no less honored than Solomon, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال له عبد الله بن أمية المخزومي : سير لنا جبال مكة حتى ينفسح المكان علينا واجعل لنا فيها أنهارا نزرع فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains that if a Qur’an could move mountains, divide land into rivers, or speak to the dead, it would be this revealed Qur’an.
rows.anchor: لكان هو هذا القرآن الذي أنزلناه عليك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the omitted answer to “if a Qur’an could do these things” is that the opponents still would not believe, as in 6:111.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : المحذوف هو أنه { لو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing Muhammad’s mission to bring people from darkness to light and God’s favor in sending him, Razi says the account turns to earlier prophets and their peoples to console Muhammad under their harm and guide his dealings with them, beginning with Moses.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك بشرح بعثة سائر الأنبياء إلى أقوامهم وكيفية معاملة أقوامهم معهم تصبيرا للرسول عليه السلام على أذى قومه

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm identifies Moses’ signs as the staff, hand, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, the sea’s parting, springs from the rock, the mountain’s shade, and manna and quails.
rows.anchor: آيات موسى عليه السلام هي العصا واليد والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم وفلق البحر

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba’i says the signs were God’s proofs and revealed books, and Moses was to explain the religion to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: أرسل الله تعالى موسى عليه السلام إلى قومه من بني إسرائيل بآياته وهي دلالاته وكتبه المنزلة عليه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim sees the parallel between Muhammad’s and Moses’ missions as showing that all prophets share one purpose: bringing people from the darkness of error to the light of guidance.
rows.anchor: والمقصود : بيان أن المقصود من البعثة واحد في حق جميع الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says أن أخرج قومك can mean “by bringing your people out,” with the preposition ب omitted; it may instead be an explanatory particle meaning “that is, bring your people out,” as in 38:6.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : قوله : { أن أخرج قومك } أي بأن أخرج قومك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj also allows أن to be the softened form of the particle of assertion, with the preposition omitted and the imperative linked to it, as in “I wrote to him: get up” and “I ordered him: get up”; he attributes both analyses to Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: وتصلح أيضا أن تكون المخففة التي هي للخبر ، والمعنى : أرسلناه بأن يخرج قومه إلا أن الجار حذف
